title: resource-frugal-prefetcher-and-thriftline-quant-suggester
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Added a lightweight workload-aware cold-prefetcher and a cost-first quantization recommender (Thriftline) to reduce per-token inference spend. Backwards compatible defaults; opt-in via runtime config.
description:
Motivation: Many customers see modest accuracy-tolerant workloads that pay disproportionately for cold-start KV cache misses and conservative quantization defaults. This change introduces two cooperating subsystems: a compact, shape-aware cold-prefetcher that opportunistically warms KV cache and model activations for frequently observed request prefixes, and 'Thriftline', a conservative cost-first quant suggestion engine that proposes quantization levels per model shard based on signal windows and unit-econ thresholds.
Goals: reduce hosted unit cost by 5-20% for qualifying workloads while keeping tail latency and quality regressions within our SLOs.
Approach:
- Prefetcher runs inside the serving runtime as a low-priority background task. It samples request prefix histograms and preloads KV cache entries for high-frequency prefixes using a capped budget per GPU. Budget is computed per-gang to guarantee fairness.
- Thriftline runs offline/async as part of Optimize recommendations: it evaluates quantization candidates (int8, int4-fast, int4-safe) against a lightweight cost/quality simulator and produces a ranked suggestion with a safe fallback chain. It emits a signed suggestions blob that the runtime can consume to apply non-breaking model variants with explicit rollback windows.
Backwards compatibility: everything is opt-in behind two config knobs: runtime.prefetch.enabled (default: false for Dedicated until 1 week tenancy tested) and optimize.thriftline.suggestions.enabled (default: true for hosted opt runs).
Checklist:
- [x] Prefetcher algorithm design and cost budget calculations
- [x] Thriftline simulation harness + scoring
- [x] Runtime integrations (prefetch worker, suggestion loader)
- [x] Unit and integration tests (local and integration with perf-canary)
- [x] Perf run and smoke tests on dedicated pool
- [x] Documentation and examples for Runtime/Optimize UI

Surface Changes (summary):
- redwood/runtime/prefetch/worker.py: new compact prefetch worker, priority queue, and budget controller
- redwood/runtime/kv/cache_manager.py: added prefetch hooks, instrumentation counters
- redwood/optimize/thriftline/engine.py: new suggestion engine and simulator
- redwood/apis/configs/cost_defaults.yaml: added thriftline default thresholds and safe-fallback chains
- redwood/docs/optimize/thriftline.md: user-facing guidance and expected regressions table
- tests/integration/prefetch_smoke.py: integration smoke tests
- examples/optimize/thriftline-example.ipynb: walkthrough

commit summary:
- Add Thriftline suggestion engine with scoring, simulator, and test harness
- Introduce compact, budget-capped cold-prefetch worker that warms KV cache opportunistically
- Hook prefetcher into cache_manager with metrics and backpressure safety
- Add config schema and default thresholds for cost-driven quant recommendations
- Add integration smoke tests and notebooks showing expected token-cost reductions
- Tweak rollout logic to support signed suggestion blobs and automatic rollback on quality regression

Observed perf (perf-canary run on r3-large pool):
- Median unit-cost reduction: 11.3% for mixed text-gen workloads
- 95th percentile tail latency: +3% (within our 5% allowed regression slack)
- Prefetch memory overhead: +1.8% GPU memory on average at 128 sequence; throttling keeps overhead under 5% for long sequences

Safety & rollback:
- Suggestions are signed and versioned; runtime will only apply suggestions with explicit rollout policy set (canary percent + duration). If quality monitors trip (eval set regressions or user quality metrics), the suggestion is automatically revoked and runtime falls back to the prior pinned model.

Testing:
- Unit tests for prefetch heuristics + budget enforcement
- Simulation tests for Thriftline scoring across 30 representative models
- Integration smoke test that runs full pipeline against a synthetic workload to ensure no deadlocks or unbounded memory growth

Docs: Added guide describing tuning knobs, expected unit-econ ranges, and how to interpret thriftline scores

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature gates
2) Deploy to internal Dedicated cluster on Tuesday for 48h soak
3) Run perf-canary + cost-comparison snapshot
4) Gradual hosted rollout: Optimize suggestions enabled for 5% of traffic -> 25% -> 100% if metrics green

Notes on differences vs prior work: unlike previous "batcher-presets" PRs, this change is not purely a static defaults update — it introduces live background warming with explicit budget controls and couples it with a dynamic, model-aware quant suggestion engine rather than a global preset. The thriftline scoring prioritizes cost sensitivity first and is conservative on quality (scores penalize any predicted >1% token-level regression).
